label: Late in the episode, a just-seen S2 state raises it (D1, D2); S1 lowers it.
short_terms: (phase == D1) * (prev_state == 2) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * (state == 2) * ep_dec
terms: (phase == D1) * ((prev_state == 2) * 1 - (prev_state == 1) * 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == GO) * ((prev_state == 2) * 1 - (prev_state == 1) * 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * ((state == 2) * 1 - (state == 1) * 1) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * (prev_reward == 0) * ep_dec ;; (phase == D1) * belief_lo * ep_dec ;; (phase == D2) * belief_lo * ep_dec
explanation: Raw GRU candidate n of unit 34 is dominated by a ramp over the episode (timing R^2 0.90; it climbs from about -1 toward positive values in the last decile). Beyond timing, the most recently shown state sets its sign: S2 raises it and S1 lowers it, at D1 (previous trial state) and D2 (the state just reached). The effect grows with episode position, so terms are scaled by ep_dec; scaling roughly doubles R^2 over unscaled indicators. The short form cannot write S2-vs-S1 as one signed term within 3 factors, so it uses the S2 indicator at D1 and S1/S2 indicators at D2. That leaves out the S1 side at D1 (prev_state is unknown on a window first trial) and loses about a quarter of the free fit. The free fit also has a small opposite-sign state effect at GO, a positive term for an unrewarded previous trial at D1, and weak negative belief_lo terms. Many large misses are whole-window offsets late in the episode (a slow, episode-specific drift) that sums of trial history and belief_cover do not capture. Belief itself adds little.
